title: Responsibility
hook: carrying your share, and a bit more

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was kavod, and your line was give honor. Whom did you honor, and what did you say? Today, a trait that has weight on its shoulders. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-eight.

Famine, and the grain from Egypt is running out. The brothers have to go back down, and the ruler in Egypt has told them: don't come back without your youngest brother. Their father Jacob refuses to let Benjamin go. He has already lost one son. Reuben tries first, with an offer no father could accept. Then Judah steps forward and says: "I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him." Jacob lets them go. Today's word is what Judah just picked up and put on his own back.
screen: `THE GRAIN RUNS OUT.` → `JACOB WON'T LET BENJAMIN GO.` → `I WILL BE SURETY FOR HIM.`

segments.voice: Achrayut. Responsibility. Turn it four ways. First, surety. Judah doesn't say I'll try, or I'll keep an eye on him. He says: require him of my hand. He makes himself the one who will answer. That's the heart of the trait: not doing everything, but being the one who answers for something. Second, the test. In Egypt, a silver cup is found in Benjamin's sack, and the ruler says Benjamin will stay behind as a slave. The others could go home free. Judah steps forward again and asks to stay as a slave in Benjamin's place. A promise of responsibility gets checked, and Judah's held. Third, the old question. Much earlier in Genesis, Cain is asked where his brother is, and he answers with a question of his own: am I my brother's keeper? God doesn't answer yes or no. He asks a question back: what hast thou done? Judah, long after, answers Cain's question with his body. Fourth, the share. Pirkei Avot keeps a saying of Rabbi Tarfon: it is not on you to finish the work, and you are not free to walk away from it. That's the measure for this trait. Not carrying the whole world, which would crush anyone. Carrying your share, and a bit more, and not setting it down when it gets heavy. Yesterday's honor treated others as weighty. Responsibility is letting some of that weight rest on you.
screen: `REQUIRE HIM OF MY HAND.` · `JUDAH OFFERS HIMSELF.` · `AM I MY BROTHER'S KEEPER?` · `NOT FREE TO WALK AWAY.` · then, large: `CARRY YOUR SHARE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: take responsibility for one thing. Settle, and breathe. Look around your life for something that has been sitting between people, where everyone assumes someone else will handle it. A shared kitchen. A family call nobody makes. A problem at work that keeps getting forwarded. A promise that was half yours. Pick one. Now say to yourself, quietly, the way Judah did: this one is mine. Then decide the first thing you'll do about it, and when. Not the whole job, just your share and a bit more. If you pray, you can name it in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Achrayut. Responsibility: becoming the one who answers for something, the way Judah answered for Benjamin. Today's word.

Your line: carry your share. Today, take the first step on the thing you claimed, and when it gets heavy, remember: you're not asked to finish it, only not to walk away. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Mussar students work on achrayut by choosing one area where they will be the person who answers, and Jewish teaching often pairs Judah's surety for Benjamin with Rabbi Tarfon's saying in Pirkei Avot.

what a scholar hears: Judah's surety in Genesis 43:9, kept in 44:33; Cain's question in Genesis 4:9; and Rabbi Tarfon in Avot 2:16.
